I'd like to learn Japanese. Anyone fluent want to help me be able to hold a conversation?

Fluent JP speaker here. A couple things; 1) you don't sound like a girl because you're not at the level where there are any differences, and 2) Japanese is language you cannot be lazy with when it comes to grammar. I mean you have to nail the fundamentals of grammar if you hope to have any fluency. It is not a language you "just pick up through immersion". As a subnote, as soon as you can, you have to get off romaji. You can't be lazy with the writing system or you will suffer later on. Good luck to you. You have a private teacher constantly at your disposal . If you do it right you could become one of the few non-Japanese fluent speakers.
Do you think i should keep using Pimsleur and Rosetta Stone? My wife says nobody speaks that way when she hears me listening to Pimsleur.

I think you should ditch both. They market to people who want to learn through immersion, which is just not going to happen with a language so grammatically different as Japanese. When I started I went through a lot of books but the one that finally gave me the foundation I needed was Barron's Japanese Grammar. The book is not very well known, and super dry, but it is exactly what you need to get started. It's also all in romaji, which is fine for your first 3-6 months. It's pretty cheap on Amazon but I'm sure you could find the pdf if you looked enough. Your wife probably says "no one speaks that way" because a lot of language programs teach a formal Japanese that is only used in very specific situations. Barron's teaches both formal and casual (everyday) speech side by side.

While studying with Barron's I would learn Hiragana, Katakana on the side. Once you finish Barron's you can graduate to children's books/comics (I mean like preschool level) to get better at reading and learning basic kanji. I can't stress how important the writing system is for learning Japanese beyond a super basic level. Knowing basic kanji let's you understand each part of compound words and even gives you the ability to "guess" the meaning of words you've never seen. Anyway, hope that helps.
